findings.description: The unit test offered as the guard for the new `needing_a_person` count cannot fail on that count. Every line `presentation.Lines` produces is prefixed with the timestamp of `at` (line 15: `time.Date(2026, 8, 21, 9, 14, 2, ...)`), rendered by `clockLayout = "15:04:05"` into `"09:14:02"`. So every rendered line already contains the characters `0`, `9`, `1`, `4` and `2`. The subtest "a round parked on a question alone" asserts only `strings.Contains(line, "2")` for a `needing_a_person` of 2, and the subtest "a round parked on both" asserts `"1"` for a `needing_a_person` of 1; both are satisfied by the timestamp alone. Concrete counterexample: change `presentation.go:48` to pass `counted(held, patchableField)` as the third argument instead of `asked` (a plausible copy/paste of the neighbouring argument). Subtest 1 then renders "round 1 is waiting on you: 0 findings can be patched, and 0 need a person to answer them" and still passes; subtest 3 renders "...3 findings can be patched, and 3 need a person..." and still passes; subtest 2 is unaffected because it asserts absence of "person". The whole test stays green with the count wired to the wrong field. Only `internal/e2e/following_test.go:178` (`"1 need a person"`) actually pins the count. Assert the rendered sentence, or a substring that includes the noun, e.g. `"2 need a person"`.

This assertion cannot fail for any input, so the behaviour its message names is unchecked here. `report.Status.Lines` (internal/report/report.go:175) appends `awaitingLine` for every run whose `Unanswered` is non-nil, i.e. every parked run, and `awaitingLine` (internal/report/messages.go:21) reads "awaiting responses: socrates is waiting for the author, or for a person the author asks, and no process of this run is running". That string contains "person". So `strings.Contains(printed, "person")` is true for a run parked on patches alone, and would remain true if `awaitingAPersonLine` and `Status.AwaitingAPerson` were deleted outright. The same vacuous check is at internal/e2e/loop_test.go:255, where "person" is one of the two things `TestAParkedRoundWaitsOnAQuestionAndOnAPatch` asserts the status says. Assert on the distinguishing line instead, e.g. "needing a person rather than a patch: 1".

The decision recorded against round 1's f2 fixed the verdict sentence but left the rest of the escalated surface contradicting it, and this change is what made that surface load-bearing: a blocking `no-op` finding is now the only non-cap escalation reason. Trace the scenario the suite already runs at internal/e2e/testdata/script/exit-codes.txtar:57, one finding `{"severity":"error","action":"no-op"}`. `scrat status` prints `verdict: a reviewer reported 1 findings, 0 of them for the person, and rated the change high risk. 1 of them hold the change while asking for nothing, so no response addresses them and they go to the person` immediately followed by `findings: 1 in total, 0 for the person, 0 to patch, 1 informational`. The same output says the finding goes to the person and that zero findings are for the person, in adjacent lines. `scrat findings` then labels that finding `informational` via `Audience`, and internal/e2e/commands_test.go:218 now asserts that label for exactly such a finding, so it is pinned rather than incidental. A session following the skill (internal/skill/messages.go:51, "hand every finding to the person") is told to hand over a finding every count describes as nobody's and as asking for nothing. Whether `Audience`/`countsLine` should report a blocking `no-op` as the person's, or the wording should change, is a product call.

The retrospective states, in the present tense, defects that this same snapshot fixed, and records no resolution. Line 25 says "`presentation.roundParkedSentence` is ... and that count came from `classified.Patchable`" and line 28 says "`scrat status` gained `awaiting_a_person` in this change; the event a person watching the run reads did not" - both false as of internal/reviewer/supervise.go:183 and internal/presentation/presentation.go:47-50. Line 33 says "It prints a positive marker for one of them", false as of internal/reviewer/supervise.go:263-268. Lines 41-45 say the two seal assertions "cannot be true for any input", false as of internal/e2e/readonly_test.go:96 and 120, which are back on `WaitForTerminal` against an escalating scenario. Lines 47-51 describe padding that was removed from both txtar files. This is not the convention the archived retrospectives follow: openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-21-the-loop-an-agent-can-drive/retrospective.md states each problem and then what was done ("`flagsIn` now takes the first `--` token per line, and that mutation was run", "The section now names both"). `tasks.md` records no task for any of this work either, so nothing in the repository says these were addressed and the one document that discusses them says they were not.

Moving these tests back to `WaitForTerminal` against an escalating scenario makes `reason(run)` a real verdict again, but the four named assertions are still unreachable in the failure case they describe. `theReviewerWrote` (internal/reviewer/messages.go:17) is only ever passed to `end(run, runstate.Failed, ...)` (supervise.go:129), so an escalated run's verdict and its `run-ended` event can never name a write. A regression that wrongly blamed the reviewer ends the run `failed`, and the `t.Fatalf` at line 96 (and line 120) fires first, which also means the `eventNaming` checks at lines 102 and 126 never execute. The author's mutation ("appending a fabricated difference to worktree.Differences fails both tests") is therefore satisfied by the state check, not by the assertions whose messages state what the tests are for. The behaviour is guarded, so this asks for nothing; it is worth knowing that the guard is the state assertion.

risk_rationale: The routing rule itself is small and pinned over its whole input space, and the two decisions taken this round did land real code, but the escalated reporting surface still contradicts itself on a reachable path and two of the tests offered as this round's evidence cannot fail on the counts they name.
